free_tier.stated: 10 GB per dataset, free, unlimited datasets per account ('you can split your datasets into small sizes'; 'we can reference datasets within datasets'). Institutional Digital Commons Data raises this to 100 GB/dataset.

retention.stated: | Published datasets cannot be edited or deleted (versioning only). A write-once archive, not a mutable store.

egress.terms: Free, public datasets downloadable without login. Backed by AWS S3 eu-west-1 plus DANS long-term archive (three replicas).

record.tooling: Documented REST API (data.mendeley.com/api/docs) with OAuth2 client-credentials; search endpoint `/api/datasets/v2/search` is anonymous. Download URLs are `/public-files/datasets/<id>/files/<fileid>/file_downloaded`.
record.chaining: 10 GB per dataset × unlimited datasets per account = effectively unbounded per identity; multiple free accounts multiply further. This is the cleanest 'per-record unlimited' shape in the niche.
record.limits_note: per-object-cap: 10 GB per dataset (100 GB institutional). Retention: published datasets are immutable and 'archived with DANS ... in perpetuity', no expiry. Read path caveat: the download URL pattern returns a JSON envelope rather than bytes for non-existent file IDs, so anonymous bulk scraping needs real file UUIDs from the dataset API.
record.reliability_note: Published datasets cannot be edited or deleted (versioning only). A write-once archive, not a mutable store. Download endpoint resolves via JSON for bad IDs, so naive crawlers must parse the API first.

evidence.proved: 100 GB institutional cap, DANS perpetuity archiving, 'once a dataset is published, it is not possible to edit or delete it'
